title: Getting started
Manifest
body:
Every package has `manifest.json`. `id`, `version`, and `name` are required. The native `ether` block requires protocol, kind, and runtime. A manifest without that block is a plain Stremio add-on. Keep reverse-DNS identity stable and increase SemVer for updates.

```json
{"id":"org.example.hello","name":"Hello","version":"0.1.0","ether":{"protocol":1,"kind":"extension","runtime":{"kind":"hosted","entry":"plugin.js"}}}
```

## Reading the generated fields
The schema table lists required fields **within their parent object**, constraints, enum values, and explicitly declared defaults. An optional parent need not be present. Absence of a schema default does not imply zero is the runtime default: consult the Go type comments and validator below. Go field tables describe serialization, not validation requiredness. `omitempty` never proves that a field is optional for your chosen capability.

Network permissions, contribution metadata, settings references, schedules, and runtime entry points are validated together. Errors identify the field to fix. See [Capabilities](/plugins/reference/capabilities), [Settings](/plugins/reference/settings), and [Publishing](/plugins/reference/publishing).

title: Capabilities & contribution routes
body:
Capabilities describe what a plugin does; permissions describe which host data it can use. Declare only the capabilities you implement. Required contribution metadata depends on the capability and plugin kind; the generated validator below enumerates all combinations and errors.

| Capability | Entry point or contribution |
|---|---|
| stream_source | Stremio `/stream/{type}/{id}.json`; lazy streams open through `/ether/open/{id}` |
| debrid_provider | `/ether/debrid/check`, `find`, `acquire`, `link`, `remove`, `account` |
| list_source | `contributes.listSources`; matching Stremio catalogue |
| metadata | Stremio `/meta/{type}/{id}.json` |
| plugin_directory | Plugin directory declarations and discovery routes |
| livetv_channels | `/ether/channels.json`, `/ether/guide/{id}.json`, stream routes |
| subtitles | Stremio subtitles resource; declared languages and formats |
| markers | Declared intro, credits, recap or preview marker kinds |
| notify | Notification metadata; send and send-test handlers |
| events | Explicit event subscriptions and `/ether/events` |
| ranking_step | Deterministic `rank_key(candidate, config)` |
| rule_condition | Deterministic `cond_match(candidate, operator, value)` |
| tools | Declared tool input schema and tool handlers |
| ui | Pages, slots, commands, ViewSpec views and actions |
| onair_content / livetv_pack | Declared On Air segments or TV pack contributions |
| catalog_provider / kind_resolver / matcher | Content kind browse, resolve, match routes |
| frontend_adapter | Authenticated protocol adapter routes |

Reserved capability names cannot be claimed in EPP/1. Ranking and condition hot paths have only log and abort: no I/O, wall clock, or arbitrary host calls. Return a neutral result when there is no useful adjustment. Consult the generated templates and route checks for each response shape rather than inventing one.

title: Content kinds & libraries
body: See the complete content-kind guide below. Start with a bounded browse page, stable external IDs, and a playable leaf. Use [Resolvers](/plugins/reference/resolvers) for bytes and [Folders](/plugins/reference/host-folders) for local files.

title: Catalogue sources
body:
A Stremio catalogue returns `{metas:[...]}` for `/catalog/{type}/{id}.json`. The catalogue ID must match `manifest.catalogs` and `ether.contributes.listSources[].catalog`. A list source can appear in collections and home rows; it is different from the signed **plugin marketplace catalogue** described in [Publishing](/plugins/reference/publishing).

```json
{"key":"weekly","label":"This week","catalog":"weekly","maxItems":50,"refresh":"1h"}
```

Keep pages bounded, handle search and pagination extras consistently, and use stable metadata IDs. Read parameters from the request; do not return an entire remote library to answer one query. For arbitrary media hierarchies use [Content kinds](/plugins/reference/kinds), whose provider sync persists items in Ether's store.

title: Resolvers & playback
body:
Resolve only when a viewer requests playback. Browse and metadata must stay cheap. A content-kind resolver returns ordered `sources`; an empty array means temporarily unavailable. File, range, download, direct, container, and release patterns have different ownership of fetching and caching; read the generated PlayableSource types and content-kind guide.

```json
{"sources":[{"id":"primary","pattern":"range","url":"https://media.example.org/track.mp3","mime":"audio/mpeg"}]}
```

Use `{secret:name}` header placeholders instead of returning raw credentials. URLs support only the documented integer placeholders. Return `unavailable` on kind items when an owner needs to see why verified bytes do not exist. Use Ether stream tickets for frontend adapters so media bypasses the plugin process. See [Kinds](/plugins/reference/kinds), [Source discovery](/plugins/reference/host-sources), and the native debrid route/error table below.

title: Notification channels
body:
`kind: "notification_channel"` with capability `notify` registers a delivery channel. This differs from `ether.notify.owner`, which posts a console notice. Declare `contributes.notification` with `sendTest: true`, supported formats, optional fields, and maximum length. Owners configure channel instances through Notifications.

```json
{"kind":"notification_channel","capabilities":["notify"],"contributes":{"notification":{"sendTest":true,"formats":["text"],"maxLength":1000}}}
```

Implement `POST /ether/notify` (the SDK notify handler). It receives the delivery request, including its test flag for a test send; return the documented NotifyResponse. See the generated router and conformance checks below. Validate channel fields and authenticate external delivery through declared network hosts and secrets. A successful connection test must mean the service accepted the request; do not report success after an upstream error. Never log tokens or signed delivery URLs. The Home Assistant example shows remote notification delivery.

title: Settings & setup steps
Events
body:
Subscribe explicitly with capability `events` and `contributes.events.subscribe`. Handle deliveries at `/ether/events`. The generated event constants below are the supported names; unknown names are rejected, not wildcard subscriptions.

```json
{"capabilities":["events"],"contributes":{"events":{"subscribe":["playback.started"]}}}
```

Keep handlers bounded and idempotent using the event ID. A delivery contains the event name, timestamp, optional viewer identity, and payload. Viewer identity is removed unless the live grants allow it. Enabled subscriptions are indexed; nobody subscribing means no plugin event-log work. Avoid polling playback or scanning the library in response to progress events. Use the generated queue and dispatch code to inspect retry behavior and exact envelopes.

title: Testing & conformance
body:
Use Studio's run and preview tools while editing. Before distributing, run the offline conformance command on an unpacked package:

```sh
ether plugin check ./my-plugin
```

The kit validates manifest fields, package references, owner-facing copy, declared routes, capability response shapes, and hot-path determinism/budgets. Content-kind checks cover pagination termination, page limits, detail round trips, declared live search, and resolver patterns. Shared kind fixtures live in `sdk/conformance/kinds`.

Mock external HTTP, store, viewer, and playback dependencies in SDK tests. Check missing grants, revoked grants, empty results, rate limits, invalid settings, and upstream failures. Offline conformance cannot prove a paid account works: after installation, run the owner's connection test with real credentials. Inspect Studio's calls and logs without exposing secrets. Package only after these checks; see [Publishing](/plugins/reference/publishing).

title: Packaging & publishing
body:
Bundle hosted SDK imports into the entry artifact. Bare package imports cannot resolve in the hosted virtual filesystem. Put the manifest, referenced settings/strings, and compiled entry into the package; do not include credentials or development caches.

```sh
ether plugin check ./my-plugin
ether plugin pack ./my-plugin
```

Keep identity stable and increment version. New permissions require owner review; removing or retyping kind declarations can require explicit replacement approval. Test upgrades and the owner's rollback flow before release.

A marketplace catalogue distributes packages with pinned SHA-256 digests and an Ed25519-signed index. Review every version's permissions, retain revocation reasons, and publish the index and signature together. The catalogue-template guide below describes repository variables, secret key handling, and artifact checks.

title: Examples & Studio templates
body: Copy a complete example matching your capability, then change the manifest ID before installing. Examples include hello in three languages, local folders, kind libraries, debrid, subtitles, live TV, notifications, and event-driven integrations. Generated Studio templates show raw hosted handlers; SDK examples show bundled or remote programs. All examples below are copyable and searchable.

title: Troubleshooting & errors
body:
| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| Manifest rejected | Field path and validator message; capability-specific metadata; unsupported names; referenced files |
| Permission denied | Manifest declaration plus current owner grant; a grant may have been revoked since startup |
| Disabled or unavailable | Plugin enabled state, required setup, injected backend availability, saved secrets |
| Network failure | Host allowlist, guarded redirects, private-address protection, body cap, upstream status |
| Folder inaccessible | Hosted runtime, owner-picked root, relative path, symlink containment, revoked grant |
| Hash too large | Use hashStart above 256 MiB; poll until terminal; retry a busy worker later |
| SDK import unresolved | Bundle imports into the hosted entry; do not expect Node resolution in QuickJS |
| Empty library | Setup completion, sync mode, page cursors, declared levels/field types, stable IDs |
| Playback unavailable | Resolver pattern, source URL, secret placeholders, item unavailable reason, viewer access |
| Remote 401 | Plugin credential or tunnel pairing; never substitute a viewer token |
| Rate limited | Honor backoff and bounded work; owner notices allow five per hour |

Generated validators, transport error mapping, and runtime fault definitions below give the exact error messages. Search a message or field name to find its source and relevant type. Keep secrets out of diagnostic output.

title: Key/value storage
Public settings
body:
Read current non-secret configuration for each request. No permission declaration is needed for your own public settings. Missing optional settings need a caller-selected default.

```ts
const count = Number(ether.settings.get().maxItems ?? 12);
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

title: Sealed secrets
body:
Hosted only. Requires the exact name in permissions.secrets and a saved secret. Missing secrets produce unavailable; undeclared or revoked grants produce permission denied. Remote plugins receive configuration instead.

```ts
const token = ether.secret.get("apiKey");
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

title: HTTP requests
Catalogue lookup
body:
Requires catalog: read. Hosted search clamps invalid limits to 100; get accepts one title ID. SDK and raw global argument shapes differ: use the exact declarations below. Do not scan all titles to answer a single request.

```ts
const titles = ether.catalog.search("Arrival");
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

title: Original add-on relay
body:
Hosted drafts imported from a Stremio add-on can ask the original provider while its address stays sealed. It is available only with the draft relay context; ordinary plugins cannot choose arbitrary provider URLs through this service.

```ts
const response = ether.addon.get("/catalog/movie/top.json");
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

title: Viewers & watch state
body:
Live viewer grants determine identity, history, and write access. Use granted() before selecting a viewer. History is bounded (host maximum 200). Watch-state writes are journalled and forbidden in read-only tool calls. Never infer authorization from a cached viewer ID.

```ts
const viewers = ether.viewers.granted();
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

title: Collections
body:
Requires collections: write. Writes are journalled and permission-checked on every call. Remote request bodies are capped at 2 MiB. Use stable collection identity for updates. Read-only tool calls cannot mutate state.

```ts
ether.collections.upsert({id: "weekly", name: "Weekly picks", ids: []});
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

title: Kind item storage
body:
Requires catalog_provider and your own declared kind. upsert/delete only work for push-mode kinds; pull sync owns its writes. items is cursor-paged. Items are validated against declared levels and fields. Unknown custom fields are dropped; invalid types reject the item.

```ts
const page = ether.kinds.items("recordings", "", 50);
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

title: Source discovery
body:
Requires kind_resolver and sources: search or acquire. Search permits indexer discovery and debrid checks; acquire permits opening content. Return a release source after choosing a candidate instead of downloading in the request handler.

```ts
const candidates = ether.sources.resolve({kind: "indexer_search", query: "Example"});
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

title: Library blob cache
Frontend stream tickets
body:
Mint a scoped, short-lived URL for one of your own kind items. The authenticated viewer must see its library. Embed this URL in the protocol response; Ether serves the bytes without proxying through your plugin. Raw hosted spelling is streamURL; the TypeScript SDK uses streamUrl.

```ts
const url = ether.frontend.streamURL("item-ref");
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

title: Storage & folders
Owner notices
body:
Posts a console notice, limited to five per hour. It does not send through a notification-channel plugin. Read errors and avoid repeated notices on a playback or progress path.

```ts
ether.notify.owner("New recordings are ready");
```
